correctness.rationale: Concatenation identity (1) is exact for all words. All reachable states fall into three exceptional, one-future-one, or multiple-one residuals; each is explicitly reachable. The suffix \(0^d1\) separates deficit indices, and \(1\,0^{t-2q}1\) separates distinct residual parameters sharing a deficit, proving minimality. Arithmetic gives \(\sum_{t=1}^k\lfloor t/2floor=\lfloor k^2/4floor\). Separate automaton minimization for \(1\le k\le60\) and 24,570 direct word-level tests corroborate, but infinite validity rests on proof.

originality.rationale: The paper of Mansour, Rastegar, Roitershtein (2019, Section 2.2, equivalence (4)) studies pattern occurrence-count automata under a finer equivalence recording all counts up to r. The present exact-k Myhill–Nerode quotient collapses these finer classes; the inspected article develops enumerators/asymptotics, not the claimed closed minimal-state formula. Other inspected primary articles concern word binomial coefficients, their deformations, and polynomial-congruence languages rather than this exact integer-equality language. published-finding corpus searches found no direct statement, but weak search recall and possible implicit specializations are disclosed.
residual_risks: An equivalent exact-k result might be derived implicitly from a general automaton congruence or unindexed paper.
Search ranking did not reliably surface the related occurrence-threshold result; therefore search absence is not taken as novelty proof.

value.rationale: Recognizers for exactly \(k\) scattered occurrences are a natural parametric family of regular counting languages. The result gives a complete explicit quotient and sharp state complexity for all k, including the non-obvious collapse of many distinct prefix count states into one-future-one residuals and a linear correction to the quadratic term. The structural classification is useful as a benchmark for automaton minimization and exact-frequency language construction, without claiming a generic higher-alphabet result.
